verdict: DoorDash grew revenue 36% to $4.5B on record orders and order value, but the bottom line shrank — profit attributable to shareholders fell 30% to $200M as Deliveroo-era costs and depreciation weighed on the quarter.

segments.name: Marketplace services
segments.note: Fees from restaurants, stores and couriers on every order, plus DashPass subscriptions. DoorDash reports a single revenue stream; orders placed through it were worth $33.1B in the quarter.

opex.name: Sales & marketing
opex.note: Marketing and promotions to win diners, merchants and couriers.

opex.name: Research & development
opex.note: Building the delivery platform, including AI and autonomy work.

opex.name: General & administrative
opex.note: Running the company day to day.

opex.name: Depreciation & amortization
opex.note: Wear-and-tear on equipment, vehicles and software — the part not counted inside cost of revenue. It jumped with the Deliveroo acquisition.

takeaways.title: Record order value
takeaways.text: Marketplace GOV rose 36% to $33.1B and orders rose 27% to 970 million. Excluding Deliveroo, GOV still grew 23% — the core business accelerated too.

takeaways.title: Underlying earnings jumped
takeaways.text: Adjusted EBITDA rose 40% to $914M, well above DoorDash's own expectation, as unit economics improved in U.S. grocery and retail and internationally.

takeaways.title: But GAAP profit fell
takeaways.text: Net income attributable to shareholders fell 30% to $200M. Depreciation and amortization nearly doubled to $295M after the Deliveroo deal, and operating income slipped to $156M from $163M a year ago.

oneTimers: The chart's net profit is $199M — net income including redeemable non-controlling interests. After a $1M loss attributable to those interests, $200M was attributable to DoorDash common stockholders, the headline figure.
Restructuring charges were $2M in the quarter ($50M for the first half of 2026).
otherDetail: Interest income, net, of $35M, plus $16M of other income — $51M added to profit.
